claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by competition between dislocation slip and rapid, strain-rate- and temperature-dependent dislocation healing or re-strengthening.
The competition between slip and healing produces avalanche-like plastic events manifested as stress-strain serrations.
Avalanche-like plastic events underlie the strength-ductility performance of FeNiCrMn across different loading regimes.
Localized weak spots or dislocations weaken during slip and rapidly re-strengthen or become pinned between avalanche events.
Localized slip bands form as part of the proposed avalanche process in FeNiCrMn.
At lower strain rates or elevated temperatures, dislocations have sufficient time to reorganize and heal, producing relatively smooth plastic flow.
At high strain rates or lower temperatures, healing lags dislocation slip and causes sudden avalanche-like stress drops.
High-strain-rate or low-temperature conditions increase the strain-rate sensitivity of FeNiCrMn.
FeNiCrMn will exhibit pronounced serrated flow under high-strain-rate and low-temperature conditions.
FeNiCrMn will exhibit smoother flow under low-strain-rate and high-temperature conditions.
Macroscopic stress fluctuations will correlate with changes in dislocation density and localized slip-band formation.
Analogous CoCrFeMnNi has an established strength-ductility balance and moderate strain-rate sensitivity at room temperature and intermediate strain rates.
Dislocation slip, rather than twinning or grain-boundary sliding, is expected to dominate deformation throughout the stated applicability domain.
The proposed slip-healing mechanism remains applicable from approximately ambient temperature to 1073 K and from 10^-4 to 10^3 s^-1.
The FeNiCrMn response is sufficiently symmetric between tension and compression for both modes to test the same mechanism.
